plan.name: Resolve explicit Go component scopes
plan.summary: This first slice of #212 adds an optional components configuration and a Go source inventory that gives every declared function and method in each scoped package directory a stable identity containing its real module import path, receiver-qualified symbol and project-relative source, with separate source and inline-contract hashes; like init, blank-named declarations receive ordinals in declaration order for each receiver-qualified symbol in each source file, even for single declarations, so every declaration has a distinct identity and can be selected individually. Loading an explicit configuration validates every proof selection and its contract, test and conformance function references, rejects duplicates and unresolved references, and inventories unselected neighbors without treating configuration as verification evidence. Manifests without components keep an explicit legacy compatibility path and all their existing checks; code verification rejects the new configuration before running tools until component evidence is connected, while model-only checking remains available. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe the configuration, its Go-only scope, ordinal identities for init and blank-named declarations, and this execution limit under D-0122, citing the supporting decisions on changed SPEC bullets; the merger must record and cite the new decision supporting these component identities and selections because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Python and TypeScript component discovery, successful-tool evidence reconciliation, the correction to project-wide assurance, evidence fingerprints, component receipts and dashboard summaries remain for the next slices of #212, with ratified model statements unchanged.

tests.name: TestComponentScopeKeepsQualifiedNeighbors
tests.says: An explicit Go scope inventories every non-test function in its declared package directories, including unselected neighbors and same-named methods on different receivers or in different packages, repeated blank-named functions and methods, while keeping check intent separate from assurance.

tests.name: TestBlankDeclarationsHaveDistinctSelectableIdentities
tests.says: Repeated blank-named Go functions and methods, including single occurrences, have distinct file-local, receiver-qualified ordinal identities that each resolve exactly once when selected and survive relocation, selection reordering and body or line-number edits.

tests.name: TestComponentIdentitiesAndHashesSurviveRelocation
tests.says: Inventory order and identities are stable across checkout locations and configuration order; source and contract hashes identify their actual bytes, and changing code does not rename its component.

tests.name: TestComponentSelectionsMustResolveExactlyOnce
tests.says: Project loading rejects empty, duplicate, unsupported and unresolved explicit scopes or checks, including bad contracts, test references and conformance references, with a diagnostic naming the offending selection.

tests.name: TestComponentScopeCannotFollowAliasesOutsideItsProject
tests.says: Explicit scope and association paths must be clean project-relative paths to regular files and directories, and cannot escape through parent paths or symbolic links.

tests.name: TestLegacyComponentModePreservesExistingManifests
tests.says: Existing Go, Python and TypeScript manifests enter an explicit legacy mode without new component selections, source discovery requirements or changes to the manifests and ratified locks.

tests.name: TestVerifyDoesNotSilentlyIgnoreExplicitComponents
tests.says: Verification refuses a valid explicit component configuration with a clear unsupported-execution error before starting any tools, instead of running the legacy gate and presenting its results as component evidence.
